analysis.headline: GST council proposes 2% tds on scrap transactions
analysis.hook: Registered buyers will need to withhold tax on plastic waste purchases
gist: GST council proposes 2% tds on scrap deals
Adds compliance cost for buyers and sellers in waste recycling
Watch for final approval and sector response
analysis.what_happened: On Oct 9 2026 the GST Council announced a proposal to levy a 2% tax deducted at source (tds) on scrap transactions. The levy would apply to plastic waste, discarded tyres, electrical and electronic scrap and used cooking oil. Registered buyers must deduct tds from payments to registered suppliers and pay GST under the reverse charge mechanism for purchases from unregistered sellers.

who_is_affected.effect: face an extra 2% cost on each purchase, reducing net margins modestly
receive payments net of tds, affecting cash flow but not gross revenue
may see slightly higher input prices as costs are passed on

sectors.why: additional tax and compliance burden raises operating costs
higher scrap costs could raise input prices but may spur formalisation of supply

chain: step 1: GST council proposes 2% tds on scrap deals
step 2: buyers must deduct tds and handle reverse‑charge gst, raising transaction cost
step 3: higher costs reduce profit margins for recyclers or are passed to downstream users
step 4: earnings reflect lower margins or prices of recycled material rise
transmission_mechanism.explanation: The proposal (step 1) forces buyers to withhold 2% of the invoice amount (step 2), which reduces cash available to suppliers and adds an administrative step. Companies in the recycling chain either absorb the cost, squeezing margins, or increase prices for downstream manufacturers (step 3). The effect shows up in quarterly earnings as lower profitability or in market prices as higher recycled‑material rates. The lag is typically a few weeks for compliance set‑up and a quarter for earnings impact.

analysis.market_reaction: No market reaction reported in these sources.

bull_case.argument: Optimists argue the levy will bring more transactions into the formal economy, broaden the tax base and improve data on scrap flows, which could attract investment in recycling infrastructure.

bear_case.argument: Pessimists contend the extra 2% cost will dampen demand for scrap, hurt recycling margins and push up prices for downstream manufacturers, slowing sector growth.
depends_on: significant price pass‑through to end users

variables_to_watch.variable: GST council's final decision on the tds proposal
variables_to_watch.why_it_matters: validates both bull and bear cases

variables_to_watch.variable: Compliance rates among registered buyers and sellers
variables_to_watch.why_it_matters: bear case if low, bull case if high

variables_to_watch.variable: Price trends for recycled plastics and tyres
variables_to_watch.why_it_matters: bear case if prices rise sharply, bull case if stable
